sources.title: Media Fragments URI 1.0 (basic)
sources.observed_operation: Web search and direct open of W3C TR
sources.governing_condition_or_default_or_except: Temporal selector t=begin,end uses seconds/NPT by default; bounds are half-open [begin,end); omitted start defaults to 0 and omitted end to source duration. Empty/reversed ranges are invalid.
sources.applicability: Defines interoperable temporal-target syntax and a useful interval convention for exports. It does not define stable recording identity, sample accuracy, UI behavior, or replacement remapping.

sources.title: Web Annotation Data Model
sources.version_or_commit: W3C Recommendation (2017); status states stable Recommendation
sources.locator: §1 lines 87–100 (data model/transport); §4.2.1 lines 805–850 (FragmentSelector); §4.2.4–4.2.5 lines 930–993 (text quote/position selectors); §4.3.1 lines 1199–1205 (TimeState)
sources.observed_operation: Web search, direct open, and find within W3C TR
sources.governing_condition_or_default_or_except: A FragmentSelector has a value plus a conformsTo reference. The model is a serialization/data model and does not prescribe a transport protocol. TextPositionSelector is brittle when source text changes; a State is recommended to identify the correct representation.
sources.applicability: Supports an optional local JSON-LD interoperability export and optional transcript text anchoring. It does not by itself identify the exact local recording bytes or justify deriving media timestamps from untimed transcript text.

sources.title: HTML Standard: media elements
sources.observed_operation: Direct open and find in the WHATWG standard
sources.governing_condition_or_default_or_except: duration is seconds, NaN when unavailable and Infinity for unbounded streams. currentTime is seconds on the resource's media timeline; setting it seeks. fastSeek trades precision for speed. Seeking clamps to source bounds and, when outside seekable ranges, chooses a nearest seekable point; seeking is asynchronous.
sources.applicability: A concrete example of why player adapters must report readiness/seek completion and actual position, and why time precision must not be inferred from decimal formatting. Local recordings normally have finite durations, but player/media metadata still governs actual seek results.

sources.title: WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices Guide: Slider Pattern
sources.version_or_commit: Live APG page; no release tag; accessed 2026-10-12
sources.locator: Keyboard Interaction lines 33–45; roles/states/properties lines 46–53; Media Seek Slider example lines 29–32
sources.observed_operation: Direct open of W3C WAI-ARIA APG
sources.governing_condition_or_default_or_except: Slider arrows change one step; Home/End select bounds; Page Up/Down may make larger steps; labels and value text are needed. APG warns touch-based assistive technology support can be inconsistent and calls for testing.
sources.applicability: A seek slider may be one labeled keyboard control, but cannot be the only way to create/edit intervals or navigate comments. Manual assistive-technology validation remains necessary.

sources.title: ELAN manual: changing boundaries and entering annotations
sources.version_or_commit: Official online manual; page does not expose a fixed release in the retrieved copy

sources.observed_operation: Web search and direct open of the official manual
sources.governing_condition_or_default_or_except: Exact annotation boundaries may be typed as hh:mm:ss:ms via a dialog/shortcut. Tier constraints govern which annotations can be independently moved; dependent annotations may update or be discarded with parent changes. Its transcription table sorts by begin time and Enter moves to the next annotation.
sources.applicability: Useful exact-time-entry and list-navigation precedent; do not adopt mouse-drag as a required action or import ELAN's tier model without need.

sources.title: ELAN Annotation Format 3.0 and ELAN
sources.version_or_commit: EAF Annotation Format 3.0 PDF; retrieved document is 18 pages
sources.locator: Tier/time-slot constraints and Figure 2: top-level tier, Time Subdivision, Included In, Symbolic tiers
sources.observed_operation: Official MPI PDF opened and search result text retrieved; PDF text gave tier rules but the browser did not expose a stable PDF line/page locator
sources.governing_condition_or_default_or_except: Top-level same-tier alignable annotations cannot overlap, although gaps are allowed; different constrained tier types share/chain time slots according to their stereotype. Multiple tiers can express richer relationships.
sources.applicability: ELAN/EAF is an alternative for structured transcript/tier projects, but may be cumbersome for free comments that can overlap arbitrarily. Verify exact tier semantics before any compatibility/export implementation.
